ShortDescription.Value: Copy & paste tool for props, trees, decals, surfaces, buildings, fences and roads: select, move, rotate, bend, delete, blueprints, undo, redo

Publish.LongDescription:
## Copaste Copy and paste for the things you place by hand: props, trees, decals, painted surfaces, buildings, fences and roads. Select a group, copy it, stamp it anywhere. Layout, rotation, heights and colors come out exactly as you built them.
**Save-game safe.** Copaste writes only the game's own components and stores **no custom data in your save file**. A city touched by Copaste loads identically with or without the mod, and unsubscribing leaves nothing behind.
## What you can select Seven filters in the panel decide what selection grabs: **Props, Trees, Decals, Surfaces, Buildings, Fences and Networks** (roads, paths and tracks). Any mix works. Buildings, Fences and Networks are off by default, so the classic prop workflow stays exactly as it was.
- Click to select, or drag a box on the ground - everything inside highlights live - Shift+click adds and removes single items - **Ctrl+click** reaches props buried inside other objects; click the same spot again to cycle through the pile - **T** locks selection to one prop type, so a box over a mixed forest picks only pines - **Building elements** switch: when on, selection also reaches props, trees, decals and surfaces owned by buildings - **U** switches to underground mode: selection reaches only what is below ground, so a box over a metro tunnel cannot grab the trees above it
## Move, rotate, arrange - Drag any selected item and the whole selection follows; hold **Alt** to move just that one - Right-drag rotates the group (**Alt** snaps to 45 degrees); **Alt+scroll** spins every item around its own axis - **Ctrl+arrows** nudge, **PgUp/PgDn** raise and lower, **End** drops to the ground, **Home** copies another object's height - **Align**: Line turns a messy selection into an even row, To prop lines it up on a reference you pick, Circle makes a circle. Grow or shrink the spacing live with **[** and **]** - **Delete** removes the whole selection at once - with the type filter, an overgrown forest is gone in three clicks
## Copy and paste - The copied group follows your mouse as a ghost. Click to place, keep clicking to stamp more - Pasted props keep their color variation and any custom color, so a blue bench stays blue. Switch the panel to Random if you want variety instead - **Buildings** paste complete: sidewalks, driveways and attached props, with construction finished instantly. **Road snap** glides them along the nearest road and faces them, exactly like hand plopping - **Relocate** (Tab): the selected building follows your cursor and snaps to the road. Click places it, right-click cancels - **Blueprints**: save a group to disk and use it in any city or save. With buildings and roads in the mix, one blueprint holds a whole neighborhood
## Roads and fences - Select road, path and track segments and nodes, then **move, rotate and nudge** them. Junctions keep their curves, connected roads stretch to follow, pillars travel along, and the game reconnects traffic on its own - **Copy and paste roads** with their upgrades - tree rows, wide sidewalks and the rest. Pasted pieces weld back into one network, so intersections stay intersections, and they form junctions with existing roads - Roundabouts, manual traffic lights and stop signs travel with the copy and are rebuilt on paste - **Delete** works like the bulldozer; a selected node takes its roads with it. Undo rebuilds the piece welded together - **Tap Alt** to straighten a node onto the line between its neighbors; **hold Alt** while dragging to slide it along that line - **Fences and hedges** - the ones drawn along a line - select, copy, paste, move and delete the same way. Chained fences stay connected: move one link and its neighbor stretches to keep the joint
## Shaping curves Select exactly one road segment or one fence and handles appear: two on its ends, two control points beside them.
- Drag an end to move it while the rest keeps its shape, or a control point to reshape that half - Grab the curve anywhere along its length and pull - it bends under your hand - A click **selects** a handle first; only a press on the already-selected handle starts dragging, so an ordinary click can never bend a road by accident - **Lane alignment**: a small triangle at each joint cycles it through center, left and right. On a lane transition the through lanes line up exactly - the highway exit look in one click
## Undo **Ctrl+Z** reverts moves, rotations, alignment, height changes, deletes and pastes, up to 32 steps back. **Ctrl+Y** re-applies them, deletes and pastes included.
## Getting started Open with **Ctrl+Shift+C** or the toolbar button. Select, **Ctrl+C**, **Ctrl+V**, click to place. A quick right-click always steps back. All hotkeys are rebindable, and the options are in English, German, French and Serbian.
## Good to know - Deleting more than 500 objects at once is refused: a removal that large can crash the game itself. Delete in parts - Placement errors are ignored while pasting so the stamp goes down anywhere (toggleable). The Anarchy mod is not required, but when it is installed they cooperate - Power lines, pipes and building-owned fences are intentionally left alone, and Copaste does not create networks from scratch
## Transparency AI-assisted development: the code was written with heavy use of AI tools (Claude Fable), directed, reviewed and hand-tested in-game by the author through many iterations. Bug reports are read and fixed by a human.
Source code (MIT): https://github.com/viktorsx/Copaste
## Credits & thanks Copaste started as a personal tool and grew into this release. It was written from scratch, but the patterns and APIs were learned from open-source mods whose MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses explicitly welcome that. Sincere thanks to:
- **yenyang** - selection, highlighting and raycasting patterns learned from *Better Bulldozer*, *Anarchy*, *Tree Controller* and *Move It*; Anarchy's PreventOverride is integrated at runtime when present - **algernon** - the object placement approach (the game's definition pipeline) learned from *Line Tool* - **Bruceyboy24804** - *Node Controller* served as the reference for mod UI integration - **Colossal Order & Paradox** - for Cities: Skylines II and the official modding documentation - The **CS2 modding community** for keeping their mods open source
### Special thanks A very special thank-you to **Biffa** (Biffa Plays Indie Games) and **ConflictNerd**, simply for being the author's favorite Cities: Skylines YouTubers and the reason this game never gets boring. Keep the traffic flowing!
Publish.ChangeLog:
Fixes for the Fences & Networks update. Hand-tested in game before publishing.
- Moving a node on an elevated road no longer splits it. The height of an elevated road is a property of the road, not of the ground beneath it; dragging a node across a slope used to carry the bridge along with the terrain, which left a step at the joint - and traffic would not cross that step. Ground-level roads still follow the terrain as before - A joint at the far end of a moved segment is now rebuilt together with every road meeting it, so a road you did not touch can no longer keep an outdated joint shape
